text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- While more and more Swedes have to rely on social welfare for their support, the social service staff appear more and more cold-hearted and unsympathetic, reports from regional authorities show. Many in need are insulted and the staff also feel neglected.

- When Swedish business leader Percy Barnevik takes over as chairman of the Wallenberg family's investment vehicle Investor he will have influence over almost half of market capitalisation on the Stockholm Stock Exchange, or close to one billion crowns. Barnevik will replace family head Peter Wallenberg.

- The car sector is ready to raise its forecast about total 1997 Swedish sales of 200,000 cars by up to 10 percent after a strong start for new car sales this year, several leading sector representatives told the newspaper. Automotive group AB Volvo has upgraded its domestic target to 50,000 from 48,000 and Saab Automobile expects to sell 19,000 cars in Sweden.

- Swedish financer Peter Wallenberg will leave one of Sweden's business community's most prestigous posts as chairman of the Wallenberg sphere's investment vehicle Investor AB . He will be replaced by Percy Barnevik.

- The private Norwegian power broker Skandinavisk kraftmegling has a larger turnover of financial contracts on the electricity market than the state-owned Norwegian-Swedish electricity bourse Nord-Pool.
- Competition will get even tougher for Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) as Nordic competitors Braathens, Finnair and Transwede will coordinate their frequent flier programmes.

- Percy Barnevik will replace Peter Wallenberg as chairman of the board of Investor at the April 14 annual general meeting. Investor, together with Wallenberg holding company Incentive and several family foundations, controls many of Sweden's leading export firms, including drugs major Astra, telecoms group Ericsson and forestry group Stora.

- The nomination of Percy Barnevik to succeed Peter Wallenberg as chairman of Investor clears the way for an eventual change in the top ranks of S-E-Banken, Sweden's third largest bank. Claes Dahlback, the long-time chief executive of Investor, is expected to assume a seat this year on the board of S-E-Banken and he would thereafter be made chairman of the bank in 1998. Dahlback would then probably have to leave Investor as Swedish corporate law prohibits the head of an investment company from also sitting on the board of a bank.
- Incentive announced on Thursday that it has reached an agreement to sell TA Hydronics to U.K. building material maker IMI Plc for 1.2 billion crowns, making a capital gain of 800 million crowns.
